subject: Coffee & Tea
title: First Crack: The Roaster's Signal
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on First Crack: The Roaster's Signal.

hook.text: At around 196°C, coffee beans crack audibly—like popcorn. This is 'first crack,' and it's the roaster's key moment.

buildup.text: Internal steam and CO₂ pressure fracture the bean's cell structure. The crack is an actual physical rupture.

discovery.text: First crack marks the transition from endothermic (absorbing heat) to exothermic (releasing heat). The bean is now self-heating.

twist.text: Most light and medium roasts are pulled during or just after first crack. It's the minimum point for drinkable coffee.

climax.text: A trained roaster judges entire batches by the sound, speed, and uniformity of first crack. It's diagnostic.

punchline.text: Listen for the crack. That sound is where coffee is born.

quiz.question: What causes first crack during roasting?
options: Internal steam and CO₂ pressure fracturing the bean's cell structure
